field.label: Enable sensors
field.help: Master switch. Start the configured sensor instances at boot and keep them running. Each instance also has its own enable checkbox, so a single segment can be taken out of service without disturbing the others.

field.label: Log level
field.help: How much every sensor on this firewall writes to its log (the --log-level flag). Errors keeps only warnings and failures; Normal adds the lifecycle - sensor identity, send mode, transport, stop - and matches every release before this control existed; Verbose adds a line per connection attempt, handshake and reconnect. Applied on Save. The log itself is on SynapseIDS > Logs.

field.label: Connection mode
field.help: Listen: this firewall is the TLS server and the SynapseIDS daemon dials in (--listen). Each instance is a separate process and needs its own listen port, which is set on the instance. Connect: this firewall dials the daemon, which works when the firewall is behind NAT (--connect); every instance dials the one collector address below and identifies itself by its own sensor ID.

field.label: Collector address
field.help: Connect mode only: host:port of the SynapseIDS collector every instance dials (--connect).

field.label: Bearer token
field.help: Shared secret that authenticates every SYNPOIP stream from this firewall. It is written to a root-only file (/usr/local/etc/synapseids/sensor.token, mode 0400) and passed as --token-file; it is never placed on a command line and never appears in a log. One token for the firewall, not one per instance: the instances are distinguished by their sensor IDs, not by their credentials.

field.label: Verify collector certificate
field.help: Connect mode only. When unchecked every instance runs with --insecure-tls and any host that answers on the collector address can read your traffic. Requires the authorisation confirmation on each enabled instance.

field.label: Peer CA bundle (PEM)
field.help: Listen mode: certificate authority that client certificates are verified against, which also makes a client certificate mandatory (--client-ca). Connect mode: authority used to verify the collector (--ca); leave empty to use the system trust store. Saved to /usr/local/etc/synapseids/sensor-ca.pem (0444 root:wheel). One or more PEM CERTIFICATE blocks; pasting a private key here is refused.

field.label: Sensor certificate (PEM)
field.help: This firewall's own certificate (--cert), used by every instance. In listen mode it is the TLS server certificate; in connect mode it is the mutual-TLS client certificate. Leave both this and the key empty to let each sensor generate a self-signed certificate in memory (lab use only). Saved to /usr/local/etc/synapseids/sensor-cert.pem (0444 root:wheel). A single PEM CERTIFICATE block; put any intermediates in the CA field above.

field.label: Sensor private key (PEM)
field.help: Private key belonging to the certificate above (--key). It must be unencrypted: the sensors run unattended and cannot be prompted for a passphrase, so an encrypted key is refused here rather than failing at start-up. Saving verifies that it parses and that it really matches the certificate above. Saved to /usr/local/etc/synapseids/sensor-key.pem, mode 0400 owned by _synapseids, tightened immediately after rendering and re-checked before every start. It is never written to a rendered configuration, never passed on a command line and never logged. If it is missing, empty or unparseable the service refuses to start and names the path; it never falls back to an unverified transport.
